To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reference state in empirical potentials should be chosen so that it is as similar as possible to the decoy set.

(1) the reference state model used in contact potentials is crucial in discriminating between the native and decoys in fold recognition; and (2) contact potentials perform best when the compositional features of the data set from which the score function probabilities were derived are similar to those of the target sequence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the contact potential reference state and the compositional properties on threading performance.
the development of information‐theoretically motivated contact potentials for protein fold recognition.

understanding how information‐theoretically optimal contact reference states are related to decoy distributions, how the reference state influences threading performance, and how contact reference states can be improved to enhance threading accuracy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
contact potentials are not the best choice to use for threading, at least not for their own merits.

the reference state in the form of the quasi‐chemical model is a good choice for protein contact potentials, and the information theoretic analysis of the role of the decoy set in the reference state is a good tool for the development of improved contact potentials.

, in the context of protein fold recognition, contact potentials derived from the quasi‐chemical model of the reference state provide the most accurate predictions of protein structure, as measured by the Z‐score, and that the total divergence is an effective measure to evaluate the quality of contact potentials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
information‐theoretically, the quasi‐chemical model of the reference state is the best choice.
we have shown that the information‐theoretically based contact potentials perform better than the conventional ones.
the reference state is a crucial component in contact potentials, which is not well understood, and that it should be studied in more detail.
The main takeaway from our work is that
information‐theoretically, it is better to use a contact reference state that is not tailored to the protein family under study than one that is tailored.
the choice of the reference state model is a crucial factor in determining the quality of the contact potentials.
the reference state plays a critical role in protein structure prediction.
